title: Report on Vulnerabilities in Private Credit
date_evidence: Report on Vulnerabilities in Private Credit 6 May 2026
key_claim: The share of private-credit AUM accounted for by retail investors (via BDCs and registered investment companies) climbed from virtually zero to around 13% in the past decade; semi-liquid/evergreen structures offering periodic redemptions are increasingly offered to retail investors, with around 75% of certain private funds allowing monthly or more frequent investor redemptions; redemptions are often capped at 5% per quarter; in early 2026 several private credit funds received redemption requests in excess of applicable stated limits and managers used existing structural redemption limits to manage them; retailisation may increase liquidity-mismatch vulnerabilities because retail investors may not fully understand the asset class's illiquidity, which could amplify redemption requests during stress.
notes: Tier 1 anchor for the signal: the official-sector framing that retailisation plus semi-liquid wrappers embeds a liquidity mismatch. Within 90-day window.

title: Financial Policy Committee Record - April 2026 (meeting of 27 March 2026)
date_evidence: Page 1 Record of the Financial Policy Committee meeting on 27 March 2026
key_claim: Retail participation in private credit remains relatively small in aggregate, but stress originating in these retail funds could spill over to other parts of private credit and private equity markets and other correlated asset classes; redemption requests have been elevated in several international retail funds and some have limited redemptions, underlining both the liquidity mismatch and valuation concerns. The Bank is examining private markets, including private credit, in its 2026 system-wide exploratory scenario work.
notes: Tier 1; UK official-sector framing of retail-fund spillover and liquidity mismatch. Cited by meeting date 27 March 2026.

publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Chairman Paul S. Atkins)
title: Opening Remarks at Private Markets Roundtable
date_evidence: Paul S. Atkins, Chairman Washington D.C. March 4, 2026 ... meta-description: IM Private Markets Roundtable Remarks 4 March 2026
key_claim: The SEC is focused on what it calls the 'responsible retailization' of post-tax, pre-retirement dollars for investors, embracing growth and innovation across all asset classes while protecting investors through guardrails; the presence of risk is not grounds for the perpetuation of exclusion. The roundtable, convened by the Division of Investment Management, focused on valuation practices, governance and liquidity as private-market strategies move into more public and hybrid investment products.
notes: Tier 1 structural anchor (103 days, 3-6m band): canonical US-regulator framing of the retailisation push that the signal sits beneath. One anchor permitted.

title: Recommendations on Valuing Collective Investment Schemes (FR/03/2026)
date_evidence: FR/03/2026 June 2026 Recommendations on Valuing Collective Investment Schemes
key_claim: IOSCO's June 2026 final report on valuing collective investment schemes responds to a recent increase in funds holding less liquid, illiquid and private assets and to increased retail participation, aiming to strengthen valuation governance and oversight and to mitigate potential systemic risk arising from inaccurate or inconsistent valuations; IOSCO is also conducting further work on private finance, including valuation and conflicts of interest, and on leveraged loans and CLOs.
notes: Tier 1 (intergovernmental standard-setter), June 2026; valuation is the second fault line beneath the liquidity wrapper. Very fresh.

title: The State of Private Markets 2026
date_evidence: MSCI unveiled its inaugural State of Private Markets 2026 report on May 12, 2026
key_claim: Evergreen/semi-liquid structures are approaching/surpassing US$500 billion in AUM, with assets growing more than 30% over the 12 months through September 2025; wealth investors now represent about one-fifth of evergreen AUM; evergreen funds have outperformed closed-end peers across private equity, credit and real estate, with meaningful performance dispersion reinforcing the importance of manager selection.
notes: Tier 2 data provider; supplies the scale/growth quantification and the counter-argument evidence (outperformance, manager selection).

title: Behind the Gate: The Promises and Perils of Private Markets Democratization
key_claim: Three forces are converging to push the retail democratization of private markets: savers needing enhanced returns and diversification, governments wanting to mobilise private savings for public priorities, and asset managers seeking new pools of capital; but to fit retail the product has to be rebuilt, because semi-liquid wrappers generate redemption pressures and structural vulnerabilities that require framework redesign.
notes: Tier 2 institutional economic research; the 'product has to be rebuilt to fit' framing anchors the structural-adaptation argument.

title: Private credit recap: Asset managers respond to elevated redemption requests
key_claim: In Q1 2026 redemption gates were triggered across the largest non-traded BDCs and interval funds: Blue Owl capped its US$36bn OCIC and US$6bn OTIC funds at 5% after requests of 21.9% and 40.7% (roughly US$5.4bn combined); Apollo honoured 5% of the 11.2% requested in its US$25bn Debt Solutions BDC (about US$730m, ~45% of requests); Ares bought back 5% of 11.6% requested in its US$22bn fund (US$525m); BlackRock paid US$620m against US$1.2bn (9.3%) requested from its US$26bn HPS fund; Morgan Stanley capped its US$8bn North Haven fund at 5% versus 10.9% requested (US$169m); Cliffwater capped its US$33bn fund at a 7% 'regulatory maximum' against ~14% requested; Blackstone lifted BCRED's cap to 7% on 7.9% requests, injected US$400m, and let investors withdraw US$3.7bn. Moody's cut its outlook on the Blue Owl OCIC fund and on US BDCs to negative on 7 April 2026; Mohamed El-Erian asked whether this was a 'canary-in-the-coalmine moment, similar to August 2007'.
notes: Tier 3; the concrete Q1 2026 gate events. Each figure attributed to the manager's own SEC filings / Reuters / Bloomberg as cited in the recap.

title: Private Credit Confronts the Limitations of the Semiliquid Label
date_evidence: Elaine Misonzhnik, Senior Editor, Investments, Wealth Management March 25, 2026
key_claim: Among non-traded BDCs with aggregate NAV over US$1 billion, redemptions rose 217% quarter over quarter; the debate centres on whether the stress reflects loan-quality concerns or investors not understanding that semi-liquid vehicles exceed their redemption caps; the chair of Partners Group warned private-credit default rates could double from a current annual average of around 2.5%, with concerns concentrated in loans to software companies that may be disrupted by AI; analysts at Robert A. Stanger & Co. compare the dynamic to non-traded REITs in 2022, when fundraising fell sharply while redemptions rose.
notes: Tier 3; supplies the 217% QoQ redemption growth, the loan-quality-vs-wrapper debate, and the non-traded-REIT-2022 analogue.
